71:The distinction between vertical and lateral confinement is useful from the outset. The material interfaces create confinement in $z$ even when the device is translation invariant in $x$ and $y$. A laterally varying gate potential $V_\parallel(x,y)$ can subsequently define a quantum dot within this well. We first determine the vertical states with $V_\parallel=0$ and introduce the magnetic field after the zero-field Hamiltonian has been specified. This order separates the physical roles of the interfaces, strain, and electromagnetic field without discarding their eventual couplings.

221:The diagonal HH and LH contributions are $P_\ep+Q_\ep$ and $P_\ep-Q_\ep$, respectively. For the usual negative $b_v$ of the Ge-rich materials and the tensile strain in Eq.~\eqref{eq:biaxial}, $Q_\ep>0$. Strain consequently raises the HH hole energy relative to the LH diagonal energy. It also couples LH and SO states, an effect retained explicitly below. These strain terms are the Bir--Pikus contribution to the valence-band Hamiltonian~\cite{birpikus,winkler,delvecchio2026}.
223:The scalar band offsets are defined relative to the \emph{unstrained, spin-orbit-shifted} $\Gamma_8$ valence edge. The strain shifts in Eq.~\eqref{eq:strain-PQ} are then included in the Hamiltonian rather than included a second time in the offsets. This convention is useful because it distinguishes the chemical origin of the well from the strain-induced change of its band character. The corresponding conversion from an electron Hamiltonian referenced to the orbital valence edge is given in Appendix~\ref{app:source}.
